package_info.package_versions: Unknown (prior to latest update in Dec 2019)
package_info.why_malicious: The Twitter Android app was injected with malicious code by threat actors, enabling unauthorized access to non-public account information and potential account takeover. This constitutes a severe breach of user privacy and security, as the app is expected to protect user data and not provide backdoor access.

execution_context.file_location: Injected into Twitter Android app codebase (APK, likely in Java/Kotlin source or compiled classes)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code accesses non-public account information and potentially enables account takeover, exfiltrating sensitive data to the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing and exfiltrating non-public account information, as well as enabling account takeover, is highly suspicious and malicious in the context of a legitimate social media app.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate Twitter app should never access or transmit non-public user data without explicit user consent, nor should it provide mechanisms for account takeover.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate apps may access user data for display or user-requested actions, but never for unauthorized exfiltration or account control.
key_indicators: Unauthorized access to non-public account information
Exfiltration of sensitive data at runtime

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is injected into the Twitter Android app and distributed to users.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of malicious code on user devices

attack_chain.action: When the app is used, the injected code accesses non-public account information and may enable account takeover.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of sensitive data and potential attacker control of accounts

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected access to non-public account information by app code
Network requests transmitting sensitive user data to unknown or unauthorized endpoints
Unusual account control or session hijacking behavior
file_indicators: Modified Twitter Android APKs with additional or obfuscated code
Presence of new or altered classes/methods related to account data access
network_indicators: Outbound connections from the Twitter app to non-Twitter domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Twitter Android app behavior for unauthorized access to sensitive account data and unexpected network communications. Analyze APKs for injected or obfuscated code, and flag any versions making outbound connections to non-Twitter domains or exhibiting account takeover attempts.
